name: Call Boss
desc:
Virtual Receptionist/Virtual Office Assistant | $14-$21/hr | Inbound, No Sales Expectations
Company: Call Boss
Industry: Virtual Receptionist / Virtual Office Assistant Services
What Your Day Will Look Like:
Think of this as being the friendly voice on the other end of the phone for small, service-based businesses (plumbers, contractors, local shops) who can't afford their own full-time receptionist. You'd be answering calls for multiple different clients throughout your shift, jumping between different CRMs depending on who's calling in, and making sure every caller feels like they reached a real, attentive person. Most of the call volume happens after normal business hours since you're covering for businesses once their own office closes, so this is a role built around evening and after-hours availability rather than a standard 9 to 5. It's fast paced since new clients are added regularly, so you're expected to pick up new account details and CRM systems quickly.
assessment:
Assessment Expected: Not stated in the posting. Application is by email only (see process below), so expect the initial screening to happen through your resume and cover letter rather than a formal online test.

There is a mention is adding a specific line on your cover letter in the job description that will tell them if you pay attention to details.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated in posting.
Required Experience: Not stated by years. General customer service experience is the real qualifier.
Preferred Experience: Experience navigating multiple CRMs or account systems at once.
Required Skills:
Strong customer service instincts and genuine enjoyment of helping people
Comfortable learning and switching between multiple CRMs
Ability to multitask across different client accounts in the same shift
Composure in a fast changing, fast paced environment
Reliable, on time, and ready to work with a positive attitude
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone who wants a flexible, remote side income and can commit to evening or after hours call coverage
Someone who genuinely enjoys talking to people and helping solve small problems on the spot
Someone comfortable learning several different CRM systems and switching between client accounts quickly
Someone who is self motivated, since this is 1099 work with no direct supervision during a shift
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who needs guaranteed hours, a W2 role, or employer provided benefits
Anyone who needs a predictable daytime schedule, since most volume is after business hours
Anyone who struggles with fast, frequent change across multiple client accounts

Customer service
Multi CRM navigation
Remote call handling
Multitasking
Client account management
After hours support
Fast paced environment
Independent contractor
Phone based customer support
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
 This one does not follow the standard 4 step process. Call Boss asks applicants to apply directly by email at jobs@yourcallboss.com with the subject line "Your New Rockstar," a resume attached, and a cover letter that includes desired rate of pay. There is no formal listed interview stage in the posting itself, so treat the cover letter as the real first impression. Total time to hire is not stated.
4-5 interview questions for this role (or points to cover well in the cover letter, since that's the actual first step):
Tell us about your customer service background and what makes you good at helping people.
How do you stay organized when juggling multiple client accounts or systems at once?
What does a positive, upbeat attitude look like for you on a hard day?
Are you available for evening or after hours shifts, and what does your schedule realistically look like?
What's your desired rate of pay? (The posting asks for this directly in your cover letter, so encourage the participant to have a number ready.)
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $14 to $21/hr, based on experience. This is 1099 pay, so no taxes are withheld, the participant handles their own.
Shift: Flexible, but built around after hours and evening coverage since that's when most client businesses need call answering. Must have availability during peak times.
Benefits: None. This is a 1099 independent contractor role, not W2 employment.
Equipment Provided: Not provided. The participant is responsible for their own computer and reliable home internet.
Felony Friendly?: Depends on client, evaluated case by case.
Drug Test: Not required.
Notes: This is a solid, low barrier entry point for a participant who wants remote work experience and exposure to multiple CRMs, which genuinely helps build a resume toward a more stable W2 role down the line. Current employee reviews describe the team as friendly and the onboarding as smooth, with flexible hours being a real plus. A few reviews also mention that training is short (about a week) before you're live on calls, and that the lack of benefits becomes a bigger factor for some the longer they stay. Set the expectation clearly upfront: this is meant to be a flexible, stepping stone opportunity rather than a long term, benefits included career role.
Career Pathway: Virtual Receptionist → Senior Virtual Receptionist / Team Lead → Client Account Specialist → Operations Coordinator
